facts.statement: Gyrodus was most abundant in Europe during the Late Jurassic and was also found off the coasts of East Asia and southern Americas.
facts.quote: It was most abundant in Europe during the Late Jurassic, and was also found off the coast of East Asia and southern regions of the Americas.

facts.statement: Gyrodus reached a length of approximately 1.2 meters.
Gyrodus had a body that was flattened when viewed from the front and circular from the side, with very large eyes.
facts.quote: Su cuerpo tenía forma aplanada visto de frente y circular cuando se ve desde el lado, también tenía unos ojos muy grandes.

facts.statement: Gyrodus possessed round teeth packed closely together, suggesting it likely fed on coral and shellfish.
facts.quote: Además los dientes eran redondos muy pegados uno del otro, posiblemente se alimentaba de coral y mariscos.

facts.statement: Researchers believe Gyrodus may have possessed a sickle-shaped dorsal fin that allowed it to swim at high speeds in open ocean.
facts.quote: se cree que el género también fue capaz de tener una aleta dorsal en forma de hoz, la cual le pudo permitir nadar en el océano de alta velocidad abierta.

facts.statement: Dental microwear evidence indicates that Gyrodus planidens closed its jaw using a propalinal motion where the prearticular sheared against the vomer, rather than purely vertical movement.
facts.quote: Dental microwear indicates that Gyrodus planidens closed its jaw in a propalinal motion with the prearticular shearing against the vomer during the powerstroke rather than through purely vertical jaw movement.

facts.statement: Gyrodus is the sole member of the pycnodont family Gyrodontidae, characterized by a depressed pit on the tooth occlusal surface and four dentary teeth.
facts.quote: Gyrodus is the only member of the pycnodont family Gyrodontidae, which can be distinguished by certain traits such as a depressed pit in the occlusal surface of the teeth, and four dentary teeth.

facts.statement: Gyrodus is classified in the Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Chordata, Class Actinopterygii, Order Pycnodontiformes, and Family Pycnodontidae.
facts.quote: regnum: Animalia phylum: Chordata classis: Actinopterygii ordo: Pycnodontiformes familia: Pycnodontidae genus: Gyrodus

facts.statement: The earliest definite fossil record of Gyrodus comes from the Middle Jurassic (Bajocian) of Scotland, originally assigned to the species G. goweri.
facts.quote: The earliest definite record of Gyrodus is from the Middle Jurassic (Bajocian) of Scotland, which was initially assigned to the species G. goweri, but is likely too fragmentary for a species description.

facts.statement: Gyrodus fossils became common during the Late Jurassic and are found throughout Europe, including France, Germany, Switzerland, Italy, and Spain.
facts.quote: They become much more common during the Late Jurassic, and fossils of Gyrodus are common throughout Europe, including France (including the Cerin Lagerstatte), Germany, Switzerland (Reuchenette Formation), Italy, and Spain.

facts.statement: In the Americas, Gyrodus remains are known from the Late Jurassic of Chile and the Kimmeridgian of Mexico.
facts.quote: From the Americas, it is known from the Late Jurassic of Chile and the Kimmeridgian of Mexico.

facts.statement: In Asia, Gyrodus is known from the Tithonian period in Japan and Siberia.
facts.quote: In Asia, it is known from the Tithonian of Japan and Siberia.

facts.statement: Indeterminate Gyrodus remains exist from the Early Cretaceous Barremian and Hauterivian of Germany, with the final known record being the species G. minor from the Aptian of England.
facts.quote: During the Early Cretaceous, indeterminate Gyrodus remains are known from the Barremian & Hauterivian of Germany, with the final known record of Gyrodus being remains assigned to the species "G. minor" from the Aptian of England.

facts.statement: The sister group to the Gyrodontidae family is thought to be the hypercarnivorous Serrasalmimidae, which previously included the genus Polygyrodus.
facts.quote: The sister group to this family is thought to be the hypercarnivorous Serrasalmimidae, of which one genus (Polygyrodus) was previously placed in the Gyrodontidae.

facts.statement: During the Late Jurassic, the distribution of Gyrodus extended to many parts of the world, with some species also inhabiting the United States.
facts.quote: Durante el Jurásico Superior la distribución de Gyrodus se extendió a muchas partes del mundo. Algunas especies también habitaban en Estados Unidos.
